title: SubatlasReadPlan
description: Which contributing studies to read, and what to ask each one. Derived deterministically from subatlas_scores.json by applying the cutoff — no model call is involved in producing it. Keyed by study, then by SUBATLAS CELL SET (the study's own cell set, named by transferred_cell_label), because one subatlas cell set often spans several atlas cell sets and is still only one question and one read. Derived, not authored — regenerate with `python -m atlas_chat.cli_subatlas_scores`.

scores_source.description: Path to the subatlas_scores.json this plan was cut from. Every question here must trace to an overlap there.

degraded.description: True when the scores had no usable partition, so questions were selected on purity alone and every overlap_shape is 'unknown'. State it in any report built on this plan: it is a coverage limit, not a finding.

papers.description: One entry per contributing study with at least one surviving question, ordered by how many questions it carries.

gaps.description: Things a reader cannot act on, named here so they are known before reading starts.

status.description: Ingest route from the CAS+ registry (candidate / unresolved / asta / local / needs_pdf) — whether this study's text is reachable at all. An unreachable study is a retrieval limit, not a disagreement.

asta_band.description: Measured ASTA indexing band from the registry, when probed.

Question.description: One thing to ask this study: what does it mean by its own cell set, and how does that sit against the atlas cell sets its cells went into.

subatlas_cell_label.description: The study's own name for the cell set to ask about.

included_by.description: Why this question survived the cutoff. 'f1' = cleared the floor on its own numbers. 'synonym' = force-included because an atlas cell set names it in CAS+ synonyms; an asserted correspondence is invisible to an overlap statistic, so on the reference project the label the authors adopted scores f1 0.027 and ranks seventh of eight. 'purity_only' = degraded run, no partition, so f1 did not exist.

atlas_cell_sets.description: The most specific atlas cell sets this subatlas cell set's cells went into that cleared the cutoff. More than one means the atlas split it across genuinely distinct cell sets — which is itself the interesting thing to ask about.

n_coarser_dropped.description: How many coarser atlas cell sets were dropped from atlas_cell_sets because a more specific claimant was also present. Where the CAS+ document has a hierarchy every ancestor of a genuine claimant also overlaps and clears the cutoff, so the same cells arrive at several granularities; the finest claimant is the one that carries the comparison. Absent with flat annotation, where there is nothing to collapse.

matched_synonym.description: The CAS+ synonym of this atlas cell set that named this subatlas cell set, when the question was force-included by one.

nested_under.description: cell_set_accession of another atlas cell set in this same list that subsumes this one. Present only where the CAS+ document carries parent_cell_set_accession links; with flat annotation it is simply absent and the co-claimants are still listed.

kind.description: 'no_publication' = a contributing study with real provenance and no DOI, so there is nothing to read. 'no_partition' = the run is degraded. 'no_surviving_overlap' = an atlas cell set with provenance whose overlaps all fell below the cutoff. 'unreachable_text' = the registry says this study's text cannot be reached.
